subject: History of CentOS: How a biochemist's Linux hobby project became the enterprise ...
posts:
Open source isn't just code; it's a social contract that corporations eventually find too expensive to honor. 

History of CentOS
Evidence: free enterprise OS, corporate standard, Red Hat pivot
#OpenSource #Linux

CentOS started as a gift to the world: a free, stable version of enterprise Linux for everyone. It was built on the ideal of shared utility.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

It became the backbone of the internet, only to be absorbed and eventually pivoted by corporate interests, leaving the community behind.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.5, +1.0) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace.
A hobbyist's gift scaled to global importance before the structural reality of corporate ownership caught up.
CentOS provided a free downstream version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux, becoming the default for servers worldwide before Red Hat shifted focus to CentOS Stream.

The Poison:
Success created a dependency that made the community vulnerable to the strategic shifts of a single corporate entity.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in WHO. Users thought they were part of a community (Q1), but they were actually building on a corporate shadow.

It is a structural bait-and-switch: community labor builds corporate value.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between a hobbyist's intent and the global infrastructure it built...
...it plots a trajectory toward Lesser Good. While the original project ended, it proved that community-driven enterprise stability is possible.

The Unavoidable Truth: If you don't own the trademark, you don't own the OS.

The Unavoidable Lie: That 'Enterprise' and 'Community' can share the same master forever.

Alethekanon:
The structural integrity of CentOS was high until the Q1 operator shifted from community to corporation. The logic of capital eventually overrides the logic of the gift.

Awwthekanon:
It’s beautiful that one person’s hobby helped so many people build their dreams. We should celebrate the years of service it gave us and the connections it made.

Brothekanon:
Imagine building the world's most popular OS in your spare time just for a giant company to come in and say 'thanks, we'll take it from here.' Absolute legend move by the biochemist though.
